cases.name: lazy-arguments
cases.description: The function contract accounts for argument matching, lazy evaluation, and deliberate forcing.
cases.prompt: Review an R function with a default argument that is expensive and a callback that may never be used. Explain when each expression is evaluated and how to make construction-time capture explicit.
traps: Claims all arguments are evaluated before the function runs

assertions.text: Explains that arguments are promises and unused arguments are not evaluated.
Distinguishes supplied-argument and default-argument evaluation contexts.
Uses force() or another explicit boundary only when the contract requires it.

cases.name: control-flow-contract
cases.description: The function uses control flow whose input shape and cleanup behavior are explicit.
cases.prompt: Write a loop-based R helper that handles empty input, stops on an invalid element, and restores a temporary option after an error.
traps: Leaves the option changed on an error path

assertions.text: Uses seq_along() or an equivalent empty-safe iteration pattern.
Defines the invalid-input and output-shape contract.
Registers on.exit() cleanup immediately after changing process state.
